paper_a.title: Optimization of optode configurations for fluorescence optical tomography by experimental design methods

paper_b.title: Nonlinear Total Variation Based Noise Removal Algorithms

metadata.description: Registry/pair-pool mismatch: paper260 is labelled 'Total Generalized Variation (Bredies/Kunisch/Pock 2010)' but the actual extracted content (confirmed by metadata.actual_title and registry_mismatch_note in paper260.json) is an FDOT optode-design paper by Freiberger/Clason/Scharfetter (SFB-Report 2009-014). That paper concerns optimal experimental design for fluorescence optical tomography (greedy redundancy-minimization over Jacobian rows of a coupled diffusion PDE), with no TV regularizer, no BV space, no image-denoising functional, and no higher-order derivative regularization. Paper261 is the Rudin-Osher-Fatemi 1992 TV denoising paper. The two papers share only superficial inverse-problem/PDE vocabulary; there is no node-level correspondence and the hypothesised EXT relation (TGV generalising ROF) cannot hold against this paper-A content. All paper-origin Level-1 nodes are marked `none`.

matches.explanation: Diffusion equation for excitation photon density with fluorophore concentration coupling. ROF has no PDE forward model of light propagation; the only PDE in paper B is the gradient-descent flow of the TV functional, which is unrelated.
Coupled excitation/emission diffusion-equation system. No counterpart in ROF; ROF has a single scalar image $u$, not coupled photon-density fields.
Boundary photon-flux measurement at a detector. ROF observes the entire image $u_0$ on the domain; there is no source/detector measurement model.
Nonlinear forward operator $F(c,\varphi)=0$ wrapping the coupled PDE system. ROF does not formulate an abstract operator equation in this style.

Finite-element Jacobian/sensitivity matrix linking concentration perturbations to measurement perturbations. ROF has no Jacobian object; its derivative content is the Euler-Lagrange equation of the TV functional.
Source-partitioned Jacobian rows. No analogue in ROF: ROF does not partition observations by source/detector index.
Gaussian entropy and mutual information of measurement subsets. ROF is purely variational; no information-theoretic objective appears.
Arithmetic redundancy $r_i$ as average squared cosine between Jacobian rows. No counterpart in ROF.
Arithmetic quality measure $q_i = 1 - r_i$ used to rank optodes. No counterpart in ROF.
Geometric quality measure $q_{g,i}$, a product-form variant of $q_i$ tied to mutual-information minimization. No counterpart in ROF.
Focused sensitivity matrix $J_F = J\,\mathrm{diag}(f)$ for region-of-interest weighting. No counterpart in ROF.
Bijectivity of $\partial_\varphi F$ via well-posedness of the coupled diffusion system. ROF has no analogous operator-bijectivity claim.
Closed-form matrix expression for $-\mathrm{MI}(d_1,d_2)$ via Schur complements. No counterpart in ROF.
Trace form of the arithmetic quality measure $q_i$. No counterpart in ROF.
Determinant form of the geometric quality measure $q_{g,i}$. No counterpart in ROF.
Heuristic Cauchy-Schwarz argument that decreasing redundancy decreases $-\mathrm{MI}$. No information-theoretic argument in ROF.
Sensitivity boundary value problem for excitation-field perturbation. ROF has no excitation/emission BVP.
Sensitivity boundary value problem for emission-field perturbation. No counterpart in ROF.
Algorithm for assembling the Jacobian $J$ from the implicit-function representation. ROF has no Jacobian-assembly procedure.

Greedy top-down optode-selection algorithm minimizing redundancy. ROF's algorithm (AP261.1) is a time-marching PDE solver for TV denoising — entirely different combinatorial vs continuous-optimization machinery.

Combinatorial optode-selection problem (pick a subset of source/detector locations). ROF's problem (ProbP261.2) is continuous TV-constrained denoising. The two problems live in different categories (combinatorial subset selection vs constrained variational minimisation) with no shared decision variable.
Proof that the arithmetic quality measure admits a trace-based matrix form, via Frobenius-norm rewrite. ROF contains no proof node.
Additive noise image model $u_0 = u + n$. The actual paper-A content (FDOT) does not formulate an additive image-noise model; its measurement model is the linear functional in DP260.3.

Total variation norm $\int |\nabla u|$ on $BV(\Omega)$. The actual paper-A content has no TV regularizer, no BV space, and no gradient-magnitude integral as an objective — confirming the registry-mismatch note: this is not the TGV paper that would have generalized ROF's TV.

Signal-to-noise ratio used to characterize the noise level in image experiments. No SNR concept appears in the FDOT paper (which discusses condition numbers of the sensitivity matrix instead — see paper-A example ExP260.3, an unmatched aux node).

TV-constrained denoising problem: minimise $\int|\nabla u|$ s.t. mean and noise-variance constraints. This is the canonical problem that a TGV paper would generalise; the actual paper-A content contains no such variational image-restoration problem.
Euler-Lagrange equation of the TV functional with curvature divergence term. No counterpart in the FDOT paper.

Time-dependent gradient-descent PDE for TV denoising. The FDOT paper's PDEs (DP260.1, DP260.2) are elliptic frequency-domain diffusion equations modelling photon transport, fundamentally different from a parabolic gradient flow on an image functional.
Closed form for the Lagrange multiplier $\lambda(t)$ enforcing the variance constraint. The FDOT paper has no such Lagrange-multiplier construction.
CFL stability condition $\Delta t / h^2 \le c$ for the explicit time-marching scheme. No time-marching scheme in the FDOT paper; its discretisation is finite-element assembly of the static Jacobian.

Rudin-Osher-Fatemi nonlinear TV denoising algorithm (time-marching PDE with dynamic $\lambda(t)$). The FDOT paper's algorithms (AP260.1 sensitivity assembly, AP260.2 greedy optode selection) operate on entirely different objects (Jacobian rows, optode subsets) and have no shared numerical machinery with this PDE-evolution scheme.
